name: parametric-dish
prompt: Benchmark task parametric-dish. Create a new PartForge part project named bench-parametric-dish: a plain round dish. Outer diameter 120 mm, overall height 25 mm, side wall 3 mm thick, flat floor 4 mm thick, open top. No fillets, no chamfers, no feet, no text, nothing else. Centre it on the origin in X and Y with its base on Z = 0 and +Z up. Generate it, run partforge_check on it, then export it with partforge_export as STL to projects/bench-parametric-dish/models/dish.stl. Do not ask me anything; this is an unattended benchmark run.

part_count.why: partforge_export writes one solid to one STL

diameter_x_mm.why: prompt: outer diameter 120 mm. tol 0.5 mm covers the tessellation's chord sag (a 120 mm circle at the service's default tolerance sags well under 0.1 mm) with margin; a wrong parameter (e.g. radius used as diameter) misses by 60 mm

diameter_y_mm.why: as diameter_x_mm; the second axis catches an oval or a rectangle

height_mm.why: prompt: overall height 25 mm; planar faces tessellate exactly, tol is slicer-irrelevant slop

wall_thickness_mm.why: prompt: side wall 3 mm. A horizontal ray at mid-height enters the outer wall then leaves through the inner wall; the span is the wall. y = 0.37 keeps the ray off tessellation edges (sqrt(60^2-0.37^2) - sqrt(57^2-0.37^2) = 3.0001 mm)

floor_thickness_mm.why: prompt: floor 4 mm. A vertical ray near the axis hits the cavity floor then the base; the span is the floor. Off-axis by (0.37, 0.53) to miss the cap's fan-centre vertex
